title: render() and screen: your component on a test page

slides.say: Every React Testing Library test starts the same way: put the component on a page, then look at it.
Render mounts your component into a div that's added to the document body. Screen then gives you queries over the whole body.

slides.text: screen is the recommended way to query. No need to keep the container around.
slides.say: The docs recommend screen. Every query is already bound to the document body, so you don't pass a container around.

slides.text: With Jest, the tree is cleaned up after each test automatically.
slides.say: And with test runners like Jest, React Testing Library unmounts everything after each test, so tests don't leak into each other.
